take_homes: Before any agent touches employee data, ask what it may read, what it may change and what must come back to a person. I can bring those three questions to the leadership team.
A reasonable use of the agent is to build a reusable check from your own company's rules, and its 'I can't tell' answers are what you take to legal, the DPO or the works council.
Closing a door, such as keeping a human on the customer-facing drafting, is often the best control. It decides which work stays with people.

monday.move: Ask my DPO and the works council representative what they need before an agent can see HR metrics. Take the three questions and a short list of what the agent would touch.
monday.who: Me, then the DPO and the works council representative; one HR partner later
monday.when: Monday morning, to book the conversation
monday.stop_condition: If the DPO or the works council says no or not yet, I wait and build nothing on real employee data.
monday.blocker: I haven't asked the DPO or the works council yet, and I don't know who would own the skill after me.

misconception.why: The module never talked about roles or headcount. 'Give it less' and 'a human drafts' hint that people stay in the loop, but nothing shook my belief that roles will go first.

one_line: The middle on scoping, signing off and asking a person was worth it. The repeated 'note on context' paragraphs and the tool-trick steps weren't, and nobody said what this means for people's jobs.
